 Order

The petitioner-accused is before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No.96/2022 of Kadaba Police Station, pending in the file of the learned II Additional Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Puttur registered for the offences punishable under Sections 409 and 420 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC'), on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant Ramakunja.

2. Heard Sri. Dineshkumar Rao.K., learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Rahul Rai.K., learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State. Perused the materials on record.
3.

In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"
NC: 2024:KHC:21015

My answer to the above point is in 'negative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The petitioner being the sole accused is seeking grant of anticipatory bail.

The Senior Regional Manager of Indian Overseas Bank has filed the complaint alleging that petitioner being the Manager of the Bank, disbursed huge amount i.e., more than Rs.71 lakhs by creating fake accounts and misappropriated the amount.
At the time of internal enquiry, the petitioner said to have deposited about Rs.51 lakhs back to the bank, but still about Rs.20 lakhs is due from the accused.
It is stated that he was initially suspended from service, later revoked the same and reinstated.
However, the police investigation is at the initial stage.
In view the serious allegation of misappropriation of public fund by the manager of the bank, I am of the opinion that he requires for custodial interrogation by the Investigating officer.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
